summary: This bill imposes a 5% annual tax on the net assets of individuals and trusts exceeding $1 billion and uses the revenue to fund affordability rebates, expanded Medicare benefits, housing, child care, teacher pay, and home-based services.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates multiple new federal programs and significantly expands existing ones, including affordability rebates, Medicare dental/hearing/vision coverage, a Housing Trust Fund, child care entitlements, teacher salary supports, and HCBS improvements. These provisions directly increase federal outlays. The wealth tax is intended to offset costs, but the legislation is structured around new and expanded spending rather than reductions.

Title I imposes a new 5% annual tax on the net value of assets exceeding $1 billion (with inflation adjustments and special rules for expatriates and trusts). This is a direct increase in taxation targeted at high-net-worth individuals.

Titles III and IV expand public coverage through Medicare additions (dental, hearing, vision), increased premium tax credit eligibility, and repeal of certain prior reconciliation provisions. These measures strengthen public program benefits and eligibility.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.

Titles II, V, VI, and VIII expand benefits through affordability rebates, housing funding, child care entitlements, and HCBS improvements, directly increasing support for low- and moderate-income populations.

Title VII establishes a federal minimum salary of $60,000 for public school teachers with dedicated funding and state plan requirements, representing a substantial federal investment in public education compensation.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill pairs new revenue with large new spending programs. While the wealth tax is designed to finance expansions, the overall structure prioritizes program growth over deficit reduction.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
Title VII includes explicit collective bargaining protections for teachers and Title VIII supports wage and workforce improvements for direct care workers, advancing worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or civil rights enforcement.

The bill's core mechanism is a new 5% annual wealth tax on billionaires, with all resulting revenue dedicated to funding new or expanded social programs (rebates, Medicare expansions, child care, teacher salaries, HCBS, housing). It contains no provisions aimed at deficit reduction, debt paydown, or balancing the budget; instead, it prioritizes using new revenue to expand spending. This engages the topic only tangentially as a tax-and-spend measure rather than a deficit-focused bill.
